subject: MerchantAI: Optimize toolkit pricing & implementation follow-up
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@merchantai.com>

Subject: Optimize toolkit — pricing questions and quick scoping

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the Optimize toolkit looks promising for our inference cost objectives. Procurement asked me to get a clearer picture on a few items before we loop in legal:

- How would you normally structure a short pilot for batching/caching-led savings?
- Do you have a recommended quantization approach for a production transformer (~7B) that balances cost and latency?
- What level of upfront commitment or credits would get us the best commercial leverage?

We're trying to decide between a 30-day POC on hosted API vs a limited Dedicated pool evaluation. Curious which you would recommend given: 50–100 concurrent inference calls at ~512 token responses, and a 99th percentile latency target of ~350ms.

Attaching our RFP snapshot (MerchantAI_RFP.pdf) — it has sample traffic and current token metrics. Can we set a time to align next steps this week?

Best,

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@merchantai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, procurement@merchantai.com
Date: 2025-08-16T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit — pricing questions and quick scoping

Hi Samir — thanks for the RFP and for the recap. Quick answers up front, and then a proposed plan: 

Short answers:
- Pilot: I usually recommend a 2–4 week focused pilot on Hosted API with a dedicated quota + prefix caching enabled. That lets us measure realistic latency and savings without provisioning Dedicated GPUs.
- Quantization: For a ~7B model we commonly recommend starting with FP16 -> int8 (k-bit symmetric) for a baseline. If you can tolerate a small quality delta, int4 + a tiny fine-tune/compensation step can reduce token cost significantly.
- Commit/credits: For pilots we offer a credits-backed pilot: $25k in consumption credits plus technical support. If you commit to a 3–6 month reserved band after pilot, we can tier discounts (examples below).

Proposed plan:
1) 2-week Hosted API pilot (we enable prefix/KV caching + batching ops)
2) Baseline measurements (t=0) + one round of quantization tests (int8 then int4 experimental)
3) Delivery of a short econ memo with expected per-token $/latency deltas and recommended packaging (e.g., pilot -> 3-month reserved)

Preliminary commercial examples (illustrative):
- No commit: standard per-token pricing
- Pilot credits: $25k credit (apply during pilot)
- 3-month commit: ~20% effective unit discount relative to list (dependent on avg tokens/month and KV cache hit rate)
- 12-month commit / Dedicated: up to ~35% with operational SLA and burst capacity

If this aligns, I'll schedule a 30-min sync with Karthik (SE) and Neha (ML) to map technical success criteria. Suggested times: Thu 8/17 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 8/18 13:00–14:00 PT.

Thanks — I cc'd Karthik for SE/ops detail.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@merchantai.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, procurement@merchantai.com
Date: 2025-08-17T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit — pricing questions and quick scoping

Thanks Jordan / Samir — quick SE notes based on the traffic numbers in your RFP: 

Operational pilot design (2-week):
- Scope: 50–100 concurrent calls, 512-token avg response, synthetic warmup to prime KV cache.
- Config: Hosted API with a dedicated rate-limited pool, automatic batching window tuned to 12–20ms for your latency needs, prefix caching enabled (expected hit-rate after warmup: 35–55% depending on prompt variability).
- Quant flow: Test matrix ->
  * Baseline: FP16 (no quant)
  * Step 1: int8 quant (no additional tuning) — expect ~1.6–1.9x throughput improvement on RTX-class GPUs
  * Step 2: int4 experimental + small distil-finetune or post-processing correction — expect ~2.5–3x throughput but watch for hallucination/quality delta on long generation tasks

Commercially, pilot credit allocation we recommend:
- $25k consumption credit applied to Hosted API during pilot (covers blown-out runs + exploratory int4 tests)
- If you commit to a 3-month reserved band after pilot, we can convert unused pilot consumption into a one-time onboarding credit for your Dedicated migration.

Attached a short pilot scope spreadsheet with measurable success criteria (latency P99 < 350ms, KV cache > 30%, cost per 1k tokens reduced by >= 20%).

Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
--- Attachment: pilot_scope.xlsx (xlsx, 12KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@merchantai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@merchantai.com

Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit — pricing questions and quick scoping

Hi all — adding a short ML/quant note to help set expectations for the metrics Karthik listed. Quoting for context: 

On Sun, Aug 17, 2025 at 09:02 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com> wrote:
> Operational pilot design (2-week):
> - Scope: 50–100 concurrent calls, 512-token avg response...
> - Quant flow: Test matrix -> Baseline FP16, Step 1 int8, Step 2 int4 experimental...

My guidance: 
- Int8: low risk. For most generation tasks with a good decoder head, int8 keeps human-evaluated quality delta < 1–2% on standard benchmarks and gives a predictable throughput uplift. Good first stop.
- Int4: high reward, higher monitoring cost. You'll likely see ~2.5x throughput on our optimized kernels but need automated quality regression checks (we can plug your prompt set into Redwood Evals).
- Fallback policy: deploy a routing rule so that for high-confidence prompts we use int4 variants; fallback to int8 or FP16 for flagged prompts (confidence thresholds or prompt-pattern rules). This gives most of the cost win without regressing critical flows.

Operational ask for MerchantAI: share a 100–200 prompt seed set (anonymized) so we can run our offline eval within the pilot window. We'll produce a short regression report tied to business-critical prompts.

Happy to join the pilot kickoff call.

Neha Kapoor
Applied ML, Redwood Inference
